indicators.note: doubly says the piece for firm is written twice in a row

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business that doubles up on its hot beverage order.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Split holding on high mount given by gold-digger

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: clove is a past tense of cleave, to split
up means on high, aloft
to board is to get on, mount a ship or train

explanation.surface: A crack opening up high on a mountain, offered by a treasure hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold-digger' suggests a prospector, but it is someone who feigns love for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupboard love is affection shown only for what one can get, the kind a fortune-hunter offers.

parts.note: 'the cloth' means the clergy, so this is what the clergy wear rather than a dress made of fabric

explanation.surface: Asking whether a garment is made of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Clericals are the garments worn by clergy, who are called the cloth.

annotationWithheld.why: Divert midstream uselessly (5): AMUSE is hidden in 'streAM USElessly', but the only indicator is 'mid' inside the fodder word 'midstream', so that word does two jobs

definitions.note: read as 'wader is', the 's acting as a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: violent suggests letters thrown about wildly, so the words end and shark are rearranged

explanation.surface: A paddling bird meets a grisly death at the jaws of a shark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two words of fodder; END and SHARK together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The redshank is a red-legged shorebird, a typical wading bird of estuaries.

clue.text: One who sells skirt and wigging

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to skirt is to go round the edge, a rim

explanation.surface: A salesman selling skirts and wigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wigging' is British slang for a scolding, nothing to do with wigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigging is a telling-off, the same as a stern rebuke or scolding.

clue.text: Carry out directions for measured amount

parts.note: to do is to carry out a task
S and E are compass directions, south and east

explanation.surface: Following instructions to give a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose is a measured quantity of medicine to be taken at one time.

parts.note: an uppercut is a boxing punch, but here 'cuts' are recorded tracks heading up, a ranked list of hits

explanation.surface: A boxer throwing one uppercut after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade is the chart of best-selling records, a ranked list of top tracks.

parts.note: a slip knot that tightens as it is pulled, used on a gallows; the ellipsis runs on to the next clue, about escaping it

explanation.surface: A loop of rope one hopes to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 9 down: you slip the hangman's knot by pleading a lesser charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop with a running knot, the knot of the hangman's rope.

clue.text: It's assumed before, for example, consuming drink

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: the word 'before' is an example of a preposition, a part of speech
sup means to drink, sip

explanation.surface: A thing taken for granted ahead of time, like having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before, for example' reads as a time phrase but together names a part of speech, since 'before' is one; the drink goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A presupposition is a thing taken for granted beforehand, a premise assumed without proof.

clue.text: … by pleading this causes his merriment

definitions.meaning: continuing the previous clue: a killing without intent, a plea that avoids the gallows
read as two words, a ..., his merriment

explanation.surface: A murderer escapes hanging with a lesser plea and has a good laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' is a link; the second reading splits the answer as MAN'S LAUGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is unlawful killing without malice, a lesser charge than murder; split up it is a man's laughter.

clue.text: Active between rounds, most of injury's contained in dressing

indicators.note: between places the active word inside the pair of round letters

parts.note: rounds are circles, each shaped like the letter O
live means active, alive, operating

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the word for injury

parts.note: an ill is a harm or injury

explanation.surface: A wound treated between bouts gets mostly covered by a bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests a bandage for the injury, but it is salad dressing; ''s contained in' links the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is a classic salad dressing, alone or mixed with vinegar.

indicators.note: negatively suggests things turned the wrong way, so the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: an are is a square unit of area, a hundred square metres
a Mac is a computer, a machine

explanation.surface: A device that takes photographs by making negatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposing' is a link here, though it also pictures exposing film; ARE + MAC read backwards together makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A film camera is a device that exposes film to light, producing negative images.

clue.text: Where van's often on line with its occupant not in the van

definitions.text: Where van's often on line with its occupant not in the van

parts.words: Where van's often on line with its occupant not in the van
parts.note: on a railway line the guard's van rode at the back of the train; in an army the van is the front, so this troop is not there

explanation.surface: A railway guard rides at the back of the train, not up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' means both a railway guard's carriage and the vanguard, the front of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard is the body of troops protecting the back of an army, the opposite of the vanguard.

clue.text: Scientific study of disturbed ego drawing crazy conclusion

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of ego are shaken into a new order

parts.note: a graph is a drawing, a chart

indicators.note: conclusion means the final letter of crazy

explanation.surface: A scientific study of a troubled ego producing a mad conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography is the scientific study of the earth's surface and its peoples.

clue.text: Event in the desert cleans hill and mountain top

parts.note: dusts means cleans with a cloth
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor in England

indicators.note: top means the first letter of mountain

explanation.surface: Housework at a hill and mountain summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust storm is a weather event of wind-blown sand typical of deserts.

parts.note: am means exist or live, as in 'I am'
an ass is a donkey, an animal

explanation.surface: Collect up a living creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate, a synonym of gather.

indicators.note: wears means has on, so the word for away contains the metal

parts.note: absent means away, not present
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A temperate metal slowly erodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears away' reads as erosion; split it, and 'wears' is the container signal while 'away' supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinent means refraining from indulgence, especially alcohol, so temperate.

parts.note: a miss is a young girl, a lass
O is a loop shape

explanation.surface: Catching a ball or missing it with a looped swing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope used to catch cattle, and to lasso means to catch with one.

clue.text: Sipped, say, stew causing stomach upset

indicators.note: a stew is a jumble cooked together, so the words Sipped and say are mixed up

explanation.surface: Sipping some stew brings on indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the food sipped, but it is the anagram signal; 'causing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical word for indigestion, an upset stomach.

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: very means actual, as in 'the very thing'
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Finding a way into the real cloakroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is a church room where vestments are kept and clergy robe, a kind of cloakroom.

definitions.meaning: used as a noun, a charm or enchantment cast by magic
a stretch of time, as in a dry stretch

explanation.definitionFit: A spell is both a magic charm and a period of time, two distinct senses.

parts.note: aspirin is a painkilling drug
G is the symbol for gravitational force, as in g-force

explanation.surface: A wannabe takes some sort of drug to be strong.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiring writer is a would-be writer, hoping to become one.

clue.text: Old style of images — not first century

indicators.note: not first means the first instance of the century letter is removed

parts.note: iconic means relating to icons, images
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: An old style of pictures not from the first century.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, an ancient style.

parts.note: a royal speaks of himself as 'one', so a couple joined by one more makes a group of three

explanation.surface: A couple joined by a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three, a pair plus one.

clue.text: Go for a lump, then split small payment

parts.note: go is energy, pep
per means for each, for a, as in 'per day'
a corn is a hard lump on the foot
rent means torn, split

explanation.surface: Pay up for a hard lump and then divide a modest fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppercorn rent is a nominal, tiny rent, so a very small payment.

clue.text: Where kids quietly rest and make fast cartwheels?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
lay means set down, rest something on a surface

indicators.note: cartwheels turn over, so the word for make fast is turned backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to make it fast

explanation.surface: A place where children rest quietly and then turn fast cartwheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A playroom is a room set aside where children play.

indicators.note: losing means the compass letter is dropped

parts.note: a caster is a small swivelling wheel on furniture
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A wheel that has lost its bearing provides help.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food or what is needed, to provide for others.
